headline: After Thursday's strong storm, expect a sunny, chilly and dry weekend with near-freezing inland mornings, then small rain chances Sunday night and Wednesday before a dry, slightly warmer-than-normal Thanksgiving.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Friday starts cold, with valley areas like Glendale waking up to the upper 30s to mid 40s and many interior spots near or at freezing. Despite plenty of sunshine, highs only reach the lower to mid 60s. The one exception to the quiet weather is a slight chance of a passing shower Friday morning on the Central Coast in strong north winds. Friday night will be chilly again.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday will be sunny and cool, only a degree or two warmer than Friday and still about 8 to 10 degrees below normal, with dry weather lasting through at least Sunday afternoon. A very weak system arrives Sunday night into Monday morning: rain is likely on the Central Coast (70% chance, up to about a quarter inch), while areas south of Point Conception, including LA County, have only a 30 to 40% chance of a tenth of an inch or less.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: High pressure builds Monday, bringing sunny skies, light offshore (land-to-sea) winds and highs in the mid to upper 60s. Clouds increase Tuesday, mainly in San Luis Obispo and western Santa Barbara Counties, as a few spots warm to 70 or 71. Another system Tuesday night into Wednesday most likely brings about a quarter inch of rain to the Central Coast (a minority of model runs show a quarter to a half inch), with only a low chance of a tenth of an inch south of Point Conception; highs stay in the mid 60s to low 70s. Thanksgiving should be dry with offshore winds warming coast and valley highs to the lower to mid 70s, a degree or two above normal.

coast: Elevated to high surf brings dangerous rip currents and beach conditions Friday, with a High Surf Advisory for the Central Coast and Ventura County coast until 11 AM and a Beach Hazards Statement through Friday afternoon for other beaches; strong rip currents remain likely on most west-facing beaches even after the advisory ends, with fairly small surf at most beaches by Saturday. Offshore, a large northwest swell plus wind-driven waves keep seas dangerous Friday morning, easing below 10 feet by Friday evening or late Friday night, while Small Craft Advisories end between 3 AM and 9 PM Friday depending on the zone (outer waters stay windy through Friday night). Seas turn fairly mild by Saturday, a weak front Sunday into Monday should have little impact, and a stronger cold front could bring wind and rain to the waters Tuesday night into Wednesday, with large seas returning mid to late next week. Extremely high, likely record-breaking tides peak Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day, and combined with increasingly likely large westerly swells (good chance of high surf on west-facing beaches), they will likely cause at least moderate, widespread coastal flooding on all coasts, with significant flooding possible if a big swell lines up with the highest tides.
watch_for: Near- or below-freezing early mornings in interior areas Friday and Saturday.
How much rain Wednesday's system brings south of Point Conception before a dry Thanksgiving.
Record-high tides Tuesday through Thanksgiving plus new large swells, raising the risk of widespread coastal flooding.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in dry, cool weather through Sunday afternoon and in Sunday night's light rain being minor, with more uncertainty in Wednesday's rain amounts because model runs differ.
